Now I have 12 reference images. Let me synthesize my analysis:

**Test image key observations:**
- Young seedlings (V1-V2 stage) on dry **sandy soil**
- Complete wilting/collapse of multiple seedlings near soil level
- Leaves are yellowed/tan/brown and curled, papery
- Stems appear thin and failing near or at the soil line

**Comparison results:**
- **Pythium_damping_off**: Reference shows cotyledon-stage seedlings on WET, dark soil — soil type and stage don't match
- **Rhizoctonia**: Bottom-right panel of the reference shows seedlings collapsing on sandy/cracked soil — **best visual match** to the test image
- **Phytophthora**: Shows more mature plants wilting in wet field conditions — doesn't match young seedlings or sandy soil
- **Fusarium, SDS, Brown_Stem_Rot, Charcoal_Rot**: All show mature plant symptoms, root/stem internal tissue — no match
- **Anthracnose, Frogeye, Downy_mildew, SCN**: Leaf spot or field-scale patterns — no match

The test image shows early post-emergence damping off on sandy soil, with multiple seedlings collapsed. The Rhizoctonia reference (particularly its bottom-right panel showing seedlings in dry sandy/cracked soil) is the closest visual match. Rhizoctonia is also a common cause of damping off in sandy soils, whereas Pythium is more associated with wet/waterlogged conditions.
